source: (cd lp-fw/fw-esp32c6 && cargo build --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --profile release-esp32 --features esp32c6,test_gpio_input) && PORT_DEV=/dev/cu.usbmodem1433201 scripts/emu/desk-espflash-step.sh target/validate/gpio-input.cap '[gpio-input] === DONE ===' 120 -- flash --chip esp32c6 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem1433201 --partition-table lp-fw/fw-esp32c6/partitions.csv --flash-size 4mb --after hard-reset --monitor target/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/release-esp32/fw-esp32c6
note: the pads are driven by the FIRMWARE ITSELF and read back through `GPIO.in_` — a self-loop, because there is no wire and no hands on this bench. What this transcript measures is therefore the READ path: the input buffer, `in_`, the edge detector, the interrupt matrix and the product's own debouncer. Its emulated twin measures the OUTSIDE-DRIVER path — the same image, with `lp-emu/lp-emu-validate/pins/gpio-input.pins` putting the levels on the pads from outside. The two are deliberately not conflated: the setup line's `drive=` word says which side drove, and it is the only thing this payload's mask set masks.

a real clock on real flash with real wait states
a scope or a logic analyser on the header pin is the definition of what the pin did

the real ROM and the real IDF bootloader printed it
real bytes over a real port
